item.title: Early voting locations for Lubbock County March 2026 election
item.description: Early voting for the March primaries in Lubbock County, Texas begins on February 17, 2026, with 22 locations available for voters to cast their ballot.

item.title: Lubbock County Commissioners ban firework sales for Texas Independence Day
item.description: The Lubbock County Commissioners voted Monday to prohibit firework sales for Texas Independence Day.

item.title: DPS confirms Trooper shot near Big Spring, flown to Lubbock for treatment
item.description: A Texas Department of Public Safety trooper was shot near Big Spring and flown to Lubbock for treatment. The trooper is in stable condition and doing okay despite his injuries. The DPS Officers Association praised the trooper's courage in responding to a dangerous situation. Updates will be provided as needed.

item.title: Border closure over New World Screwworm threat ripples across U.S. beef industry
item.description: The closure of the southern border to live Mexican cattle imports, prompted by concerns over the New World screwworm, is sending shockwaves through the U.S. beef industry, affecting producers, rural communities and consumers, alike.

item.title: Lubbock County Commissioners set to revise game room ordinance
item.description: Monday's agenda included specific requests, such as funding for 4th on Broadway, which plans to benefit the arts in our community. As well as deciding against the selling of fireworks for Texas Independence Day. However, commissioners spent much of their time on the discussion regarding game room regulations in the county.

item.title: Texas lawmakers, firefighters say Panhandle is more prepared for wildfires
item.description: State lawmakers in Texas have made progress in preventing and fighting wildfires since the Smokehouse Creek fire two years ago, by passing bills to allocate more funding to departments in high wildfire risk areas and removing the cap for funding volunteer fire departments.

item.title: 'I sent an email and look where it got me': Teen's letter inspires Rep. Jasmine Crockett's Lubbock visit
item.description: Fifteen-year-old Brooklyn wrote an email to Texas Rep. Jasmine Crockett in hopes that she would make her way to the Hub City as part of her Texas Tough Campaign, a tour through the Lone Star State, to promote her campaign for the U.S. Senate seat.
